source_text: Apostolica sententia, qua notat haereticos prohibentes nubere , etiam me - asseris - tangi hominem sufficere ingenitis sibi motibus dare leges Post adventum Christi turpia esse coniugia
pass_a_gloss: Apostolica position, where notat heretics prohibentes nubere, also me - asseris - tangi human-being sufficere ingenitis to-himself motibus to-give laws after adventum of-Christ turpia to-be marriages.

lemmas.lexica: LS lex; Blaise lex Dei / sacred Law

pass_b_english: Augustine reports Julian applied to him the apostolic condemnation of heretics ‘forbidding marriage’ (1 Timothy 4:3), alleging that his position was: ‘After Christ’s coming, marriages are shameful.’
A human being is sufficient to lay down laws for his inborn impulses.

choices.why: Julian means Scripture's legal/authoritative witness, especially the divine Law as teacher of justice.
rejected: natural law (unless the sentence is philosophical)

choices.why: Paul in Julian's citations; keep Apostle not 'Paul' unless Paulus is written.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

bible_refs.note: Linked from Julian's wording or a clear allusion in the excerpt.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
